messages:
Maria: Heads-up — noticed a regression in production Mixtral runs after we enabled KV prefetch for low-latency paths. p50 increased ~12% and p99 ~28% on several customer traces.
Kai: Which model/config? bit more detail pls
Maria: Mixtral-8x7b (official) w/ head_dim=12. We had been using the prefetch+continuous-kv codepath. Regression popped when routing selected Triton SDPA kernel instead of FlashAttention for inference requests.
Anil: Why would SDPA be picked for a head_dim of 12? flash usually handles non-multiples by padding or fallback, right?
Maria: That's the weird bit. Our kernel-selection heuristic picks Flash when head_dim%8==0 else Triton SDPA for safety. But profiling shows SDPA was slower here and also emitting some mask-offset warnings in trace.
Sasha: Paste the profile output?
Maria: Here are aggregated traces (short):
```
kernel, total_us, calls
FlashAttention_forward, 0, 0
Triton_SDPA_forward, 45230, 1245
kv_prefetch_copy, 12040, 1245
kv_apply_mask, 2400, 1245
other_kernels, 8300, 1245
```
Maria: On the same traces with prefetch disabled:
```
FlashAttention_forward, 37800, 1245
kv_prefetch_copy, 0, 0
kv_apply_mask, 1800, 1245
other_kernels, 7600, 1245
```
Maria: So Flash path appears faster overall when it runs, but selection went SDPA.
Yuko: Could this be coming from our head-dim parity check? Mixtral's head_dim=12 is divisible by 4 but not 8. IIRC Flash kernel we ship expects 8/16 alignment to avoid internal padding codepath.
Anil: Also saw a masking bug earlier when mask range & kv cache offset wrap happened — could be related. The SDPA path applies mask logic differently and our KV prefetch introduces an extra offset adjustment that wasn't accounted for when headdim != 8/16.
Kai: Can someone share the routing decision log snippet? our runtime logs kernel pick reasons.
Maria: From the request debug: 
```
[route] model: mixtral-8x7b  head_dim=12  seq=1024
[kernel_pick] candidates=[FlashAttention,Triton_SDPA] scores=[0.42,0.58] reason=heuristic(headdim_align=4)
[kv] prefetch=enabled  policy=continuous
```
Maria: Score calc gives Triton_SDPA slight edge because it thinks Flash will need extra workspace/pad cost for 12.
Sasha: But prof shows Flash would be better. So our cost model is off for this architecture/hw combo.
Yuko: Which GPU type? A100-80GB? V100? different kernel perf characteristics
Maria: This was on A100 L4 (on Dedicated), same as other Mixtral runs.
Anil: Actionable items: 1) adjust heuristic to run a quick micro-probe (1-2 warmup batches) to empirically pick kernel per model+hw. 2) disable KV prefetch for non-8-multiple head dims until mask offset logic validated. 3) add targeted unit test for mask+kv offset when head_dim%8!=0.
Kai: I like the micro-probe idea — cheap and gives real numbers. We should limit to first N requests per pod and cache the result for that model+hw tuple.
Sasha: For short term, can we flip policy to prefer Flash when head_dim%4==0 and head_dim<16? empirically seems fine for 12.
Maria: We tested a canary with forced Flash on a small shard — p50 down 9% vs current, p99 down 16%. So yes, preferring Flash helps here.
perf-bot: Canary deployment 2024-05-12T18:30 -> mixtral-canary-12-flash: success metrics: p50 -9.1%, p99 -15.8%, error_rate +0.01% (no functional regressions detected)
Yuko: Good. I’ll open a runtime PR to: implement micro-probe, add cache key = (model, hw, head_dim_mod), and gate kv-prefetch when head_dim%8!=0. Also will add mask offset assertions.
Anil: Add a test that replays a trace with a wrapped KV offset and asserts identical logits between Flash vs Triton with prefetch off/on.
Kai: Assignments? Maria take follow-up on customer impact & rollback timeline. Yuko take runtime PR + tests. Sasha own canary monitors and perf dashboard update.
Maria: Will ping CS+account owners, we can toggle customer-level routing if needed.
Sasha: I'll also add a short note to runbook about odd head_dim behavior and temporary workaround flags.
Maria: Thanks — let's aim for a staged rollout after CI. Will post updates here when PRs land. :thumbsup:
Kai: Thanks all.
